children: Over a century ago, JK Cotton spun textiles out of Kanpur, before the company diversified into other businesses. Renamed JK Urbanscapes in 2023, the 104-year-old company, which attempted a brief revival of its textile business in 2009, is now betting on a bigger prize: turning old industrial and mill land into hospitality and urban real estate.

The foundations of this big pivot are taking shape in Kanpur — the karmabhoomi of JK Group Founder Lala Kamlapat Singhania —alongside legacy land parcels across northern and eastern India. Led by fifth-generation scion Abhishek Singhania, the company is investing ₹965 crore in hospitality and has sewn partnerships with Indian Hotels Company (IHCL) and Minor Hotels to develop 650 keys across Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Bihar, West Bengal, and Haryana. Alongside it, sits a real estate pipeline with an estimated topline of ₹4,400 crore.

The real estate projects are a mix of residential townships, senior living and mixed-use developments. Take JK Vera, a mixed-use township on Kamlapat Singhania Road (Kalpi Road) in Kanpur, an approximately 50-acre redevelopment being developed in phases. It will consist of the Taj Hotel and Residences with 150 keys and 14 residences, a 100-key Ginger hotel, some 1.6 lakh sq ft of workspaces and high-street retail. “This will be the first Taj hotel in Kanpur,” said Maneesh Mansingka, Joint Managing Director of JK Urbanscapes. He said the hotel is expected to be ready by 2030. To lead the hospitality vertical, the company has hired former Taj hand Jayanta Das.

The company’s residential portfolio includes the completed 25-acre Emerald Garden township in Kanpur and an under-development 90-acre Emerald Gulistan plotted residential township. In Gurugram, its Advait Senior Living project for which it has partnered with Manish Periwal’s Pioneer Urban Land, features 164 residences across four towers, spread over 3.5 lakh sq ft.

Singhania said that the group holds plenty of land parcels from its legacy businesses, with clear ownership deeds, for future development. For instance, he said in West Bengal, at Rishra, where the old JK Steel mill stood, it is evaluating a high-quality mixed-use development centred around a major plotted residential township. In Kota, it has 37 acres of land parcel that was earlier part of JK Synthetics where it is evaluating a suitable development.
The chairman also pointed how JK Urbanscapes Developers has appointed TQ Cert Services, a Tata Project subsidiary, as Project Management Consultant across its developments lending strong oversight.

Mansingka revealed how the hospitality portfolio of JK Urbanscapes’ spanned six projects across Bodh Gaya, Mussoorie, Kanpur, Dehradun and Darjeeling, covering a mix of luxury hotels, premium resorts and destination-led hospitality assets. In Darjeeling, the company had acquired the Tindharia tea estate through which the Darjeeling Himalayan Toy Train runs. Here the 70-key Anantara luxury retreat project with Minor hotels was coming up, expected to be ready by 2031.
Singhania described how the family’s own heritage property would be brought into the hospitality fold with the 41-key Kamla Castle IHCL SeleQtions in Mussoorie that is expected to launch in 2029.
The company is also exploring future hotel developments in Rishikesh, Jaipur and Kota, extending its development focus across pilgrimage, leisure and cultural destinations.
For the Singhanias, the loom may have stopped spinning, but the land is weaving a new story.

title: From cotton mills to cityscapes – How the Singhanias are unlocking legacy land
